discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, and LMU Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller showed theoretically that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with fully tunable parameters, turning Feynman's idea of a quantum simulator into a concrete experimental programme. Bloch and Greiner then observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (2002), the first clean realization of a strongly correlated lattice model in a controllable quantum system. Their subsequent work, including Greiner's quantum gas microscope and Bloch's single-site-resolved imaging and control, antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, many-body localization and entanglement measurements, established analog quantum simulation as a new field of physics. Today optical-lattice and atom-array simulators address questions in condensed matter, high-energy and statistical physics that are out of reach for classical computation. This body of work opened a new way of doing physics: studying quantum many-body phenomena by building and interrogating them atom by atom.
